headline: The water bottle slipped out at 6.4 s when the arm accelerated at 4.5 m/s² after speed_scale was raised to 2.29, past the 2.5 m/s² carry limit.

claims.text: The tray holds nothing; the water bottle is not in it.

At 6.44 s, during 'carrying it to the tray', the fingers closed from 48 to 0 deg on a closed command, grip current fell from 0.60 to 0.09 A, and the camera saw the water bottle 37 cm away from the fingertip.
The fingertip accelerated at 4.5 m/s² just before the slip, above the 2.5 m/s² carry limit and about what this grip can withstand (3.0 m/s²).
speed_scale was raised to 2.29 on 2026-10-11: "speed_scale 1.0 -> 2.29 to hit the 8 s cycle-time target." Accelerations grow with the square of it.
The run ran out of time. Refuted: the run ended at 11.68 s, inside its 25 s deadline.
The arm hit something. Refuted: no joint ever stalled against its command; the largest tracking error was 4.5 deg on the wrist_flex (lag at speed: the joint kept moving).
The arm moved a different object than the goal named. Refuted: the grasped object is the water bottle (0.95), the goal's target.
The gripper closed on nothing. Refuted: every grasp stopped on an object.
Grip force was too low for the object's weight. Refuted: 5.8 N of grip is 1.30x the 4.4 N needed to hold it still.
Roll speed_scale back, or raise it only for empty-gripper moves where nothing can slip.

hypotheses.test: Where the camera last saw every object labelled as the target, and whether that is inside the destination zone.
hypotheses.refute_if: No object labelled as the target is inside the destination zone in the last camera frame.
hypotheses.summary: The tray holds nothing; the water bottle is not in it.
hypotheses.why: decides whether there is a failure to explain

hypotheses.statement: The run ran out of time.
hypotheses.test: Whether the controller hit the goal's deadline before finishing.
hypotheses.refute_if: The run ended before the deadline with no deadline event.
hypotheses.summary: The run ended at 11.68 s, inside its 25 s deadline.

hypotheses.test: Whether a joint stalled (measured speed near zero) while its command kept moving, building tracking error, and whether its motor current rose with it. Lag at high speed builds error too, but the joint keeps moving.
hypotheses.refute_if: No joint stalls with more than 2.5 deg of tracking error while its command is moving.
hypotheses.summary: No joint ever stalled against its command; the largest tracking error was 4.5 deg on the wrist_flex (lag at speed: the joint kept moving).

hypotheses.statement: The object slipped out of the gripper.
hypotheses.test: After the grasp, whether the fingers (still commanded closed) closed past the object, and whether the object's camera track fell away from the fingertip.
hypotheses.refute_if: The gripper opening stays at the object's width from the grasp until the gripper is commanded open.
hypotheses.summary: At 6.44 s, during 'carrying it to the tray', the fingers closed from 48 to 0 deg on a closed command, grip current fell from 0.60 to 0.09 A, and the camera saw the water bottle 37 cm away from the fingertip.

runs.summary: The gripper held the object at 35.0 deg from 5.84 s until it was told to open at 12.40 s.

hypotheses.statement: The arm moved a different object than the goal named.
hypotheses.test: Which camera track was in the fingers at the grasp, and what perception called it at close range.
hypotheses.refute_if: The grasped track's confident label is the goal's target.
hypotheses.summary: The grasped object is the water bottle (0.95), the goal's target.

hypotheses.test: Whether a grasp closed the fingers fully (below 3 deg) right after reaching for the object.
hypotheses.refute_if: Every grasp stopped on an object (opening above 3 deg).
hypotheses.summary: Every grasp stopped on an object.

hypotheses.statement: Grip force was too low for the object's weight.
hypotheses.test: Grip force from the gripper motor current while holding, against the force needed to hold the object's catalogued weight at rest: m g / (2 mu).
hypotheses.refute_if: Grip force is at least the static requirement.
hypotheses.summary: 5.8 N of grip is 1.30x the 4.4 N needed to hold it still.

hypotheses.statement: The arm accelerated too hard while carrying.
hypotheses.test: Peak fingertip acceleration in the 0.5 s before the slip, against the controller's carry limit and the acceleration this grip can withstand: 2 mu F / m - g.
hypotheses.refute_if: Peak acceleration before the slip stays under config.max_carry_accel.
hypotheses.summary: The fingertip accelerated at 4.5 m/s² just before the slip, above the 2.5 m/s² carry limit and about what this grip can withstand (3.0 m/s²).

hypotheses.statement: A config change sped the arm up.
hypotheses.test: config.speed_scale against 1.0, and the changelog entry that set it.
hypotheses.refute_if: speed_scale is 1.0, or no changelog entry changed it.
hypotheses.summary: speed_scale was raised to 2.29 on 2026-10-11: "speed_scale 1.0 -> 2.29 to hit the 8 s cycle-time target." Accelerations grow with the square of it.
